test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which sector's demand for and consumption of water is highest in our country?
solution:
The correct answer is the __Agricultural Sector__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Agricultural Sector __has a greater consumption share of water in India.
 
• It accounts for approximately 90% of 761,000 billion litres of annual freshwater withdrawals in the country.
 
• Per capita consumption of water in the agriculture sector ranges from 4,913 to 5,800 kilolitres per capita per year.
 
• The inequity in irrigation water allocation among crops, with more than 60% being diverted for the cultivation of two crops- sugar cane and paddy adds to the distress.
 
• Under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, financial assistance of up to 55% is available for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers for the adoption of micro-irrigation systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__ **

 
• As per the Central Water Commission, 85.3% of the total water consumed was for agriculture in the year 2000.
 
• This is likely to decrease to 83.3% by 2025.
 
• India does not spend any money in conserving water consumed in agriculture. Surprisingly, water conservation takes place in the industry and utility sectors, both of which consume less than 5% of the nation’s water.
